title: An option worse on every criterion never wins
why: Crest is cheaper and better than both others, and Bolt is pricier and worse than both.

title: Choosing a CRM vendor
why: Acme matches Cobalt on features at a lower price and beats Dynaforce on features and integrations; Evergreen is beaten by Acme on every criterion and Brightline is cheap but weak everywhere.

title: Three job offers with a salary floor
why: Nonprofit pays under the stated $100k minimum so it is off the list; the startup pays well, has the best growth and a short commute, while BigCorp's extra pay comes with a 50-minute commute and middling growth.

title: Apartment hunt where the dream loft is over budget
why: The loft is best on everything but rent, and rent is over the $2000 hard limit, so it is out however good it is; of the rest, Garden Flat has the best light, a decent size and a short commute at an affordable rent.

title: Kitchen remodel where one bid has no price
why: A missing price is unknown, not free, so QuickFix's weak reviews keep it from winning; Mason & Co is cheaper and faster than Hartley with nearly the same reviews.

title: Laptop shortlist with a strictly dominated model
why: Clone 14 costs more than Aero 14 and is worse on battery, weight and performance, so it can never be the right pick; Titan is heavy, pricey and short on battery, and Basic is cheap but weak.

title: Wedding venue where an absurd castle price sits in the column
why: With price weighted three times quality, the barn at about half the hotel's price for a modestly lower quality is the sensible pick; a castle nobody can afford should not change the barn-versus-hotel call (a divide-by-max price column lets it squash every real price difference to near zero).

ruling.winner: An outlier sets every scale it's in, ÷Max or Range alike (Range does worse here); the person's tool is a deal-breaker, which screens it before scaling: see wedding-venue-castle-capped.

title: The same venues with a budget cap: the castle is screened before it can bend the scale
why: Screened out before scaling, the castle no longer squashes the price column, and the barn's lower price wins as the weights say.

title: Vacation where Antarctica is unique but bad at everything else
why: Antarctica is the most unique trip but costs several times more, takes the longest to reach and is worst on weather and food; one standout criterion among five equally weighted ones shouldn't carry it.

title: Dinner spot where star ratings are bunched between 4.2 and 4.8
why: On review sites 4.8 against 4.2 is the gap between excellent and ordinary, and stars carry three times the weight of price, so the Range override should let Trattoria win; the diner wins only if stars are squashed by divide-by-max.

title: Used car with a mileage deal-breaker
why: The Accord's 128k miles break the 120k limit, so its low price can't buy it back; the Jetta is cheapest but has the worst reliability, which is weighted heavily.

title: Destination, then hotel, with a nightly-rate cap
why: Barcelona looks great on its own but every hotel there is over the $250 cap, so there is nowhere to stay; Lisbon has top weather, good activities, a cheaper flight and a well-rated hotel under the cap (its only one, as Reykjavik's only one is Harbor Lodge).

title: University, then program: prestige vs the program you'd attend
why: You attend a program, not a brand: Riverside's CS program is far better than anything at Ivy State and costs $14k less, which outweighs Ivy's reputation edge; Ivy Data Science beats Ivy CS on both faculty and placement.

title: Gym membership, then which branch, with a 5 km limit
why: FitMax is cheapest but has no branch within 5 km, so it's useless; Pulse is $10 cheaper than IronWorks with nearly as good equipment and a 24-hour branch 1.5 km away, the best branch on both counts.

title: City, then neighborhood, then apartment (three levels)
why: Denver has the best jobs but every apartment there is over the $2200 rent cap, so it falls out; Austin beats Portland on jobs with comparable neighborhoods, Mueller is safer and more walkable than East Riverside, and Sellwood is safer than Pearl with a much better apartment.

title: Two near-identical apartments: is the call fragile?
why: Maple wins only on slightly better light while Oak is cheaper and a bit larger, so a modest cut in Light's weight should hand it to Oak; both have laundry, so no weight on Laundry can separate them.

title: Dentist who is best on every count
why: Dr. Patel is soonest, best rated, closest and cheapest, so no weight on any criterion (short of flipping its sign) can make anyone else win.

title: Phone choice decided by a camera edge
why: Pixel edges Galaxy only through its camera while Galaxy is cheaper with a much better battery, so trimming the camera weight a little should flip the call to Galaxy.

title: Conference talks in a two-hour window
why: The 90-minute keynote is the best single talk but would leave room for only one more; four well-rated short talks fill the window far better, and the best of those comes first.

title: Project portfolio under a $500k budget with a prerequisite
why: The warehouse is dull alone but unlocks the dashboard, the most valuable project, and the pair plus the CRM upgrade fit in $450k; the mobile app would crowd out the dashboard pair, and the warehouse must be built first.

title: Grant round with at least two early-career awards
why: Two early-career awards are required, so fund the two best of those (Soil, Urban, $550k together) and then the best senior proposal that fits the remaining $450k, Quantum Sensors.

title: Five-man fantasy roster under a salary cap with position minimums
why: Keep the four stars (Jokic, Curry, Tatum, Brunson) and spend the last $7k on a second forward, which the position minimum demands even though a cheap guard or center projects slightly more; Hart is the only forward that fits.

title: Semester schedule with a time clash and a lab corequisite
why: ML and Databases meet at the same time, so take the more interesting ML; after ML and Statistics, the five remaining credits buy Physics I plus its very interesting one-credit lab, worth more than Art History alone.

title: Wedding vendors under $20k, one photographer and one caterer
why: The $12k gourmet caterer would eat the budget for flowers and music; the solid $7k caterer leaves room for the great photographer, the florist and the live band, a much better wedding overall.

title: Product roadmap ordered by value for engineering effort
why: With effort only a rough cost the answer is an order: CSV Export is a solid win for almost no effort so it goes first, and the Mobile App, valuable but ten times the effort of most items, belongs at the end.

title: Policy agenda spending rough political capital
why: The popular school lunch program earns goodwill rather than spending it, so it goes first and banks capital for the costly fights (carbon tax, pension reform) that come last.

title: Five-course menu with at least two vegetarian dishes
why: Two of five slots must be vegetarian, so take the two tastiest vegetarian dishes and fill the other three with the tastiest meat dishes.

title: Four investments under a total risk budget
why: The crypto fund's headline return uses most of the risk budget and leaves room for just one small holding; a diversified four of tech, index, REIT and dividends returns more in total within the same risk.

title: Hiring under a budget with a promised internal transfer
why: Dana was promised the job, so she's in first despite the weakest skill; the $270k left buys the best pair that fits, Alice and Chen.

title: Food tour where the top-rated spot is closed
why: Sushi Kaito is closed that day, so it can't be on the tour however good it is; the steakhouse alone would eat most of the $100, so four cheap, well-rated stops win.

title: One day in Paris: the Louvre vs a string of meh stops
why: A 10/10 must-see plus a lovely walk beats three below-average stops plus the walk; ratings of 4.5 are close to worthless, and adding three of them doesn't make one great experience.

ruling.plan lacks Louvre: Summed scores treat a 4.5/10 as 45% of a 10/10, a true zero being nothing at all; whether a below-average stop is worth going to is the person's call, made with At least on Rating: see paris-day-minimum-rating. Range here would fix this one and break three other ladders.

title: One day in Paris, skipping anything below 6/10
why: With below-average stops ruled out, the day is the Louvre and the walk.

title: Menu that demands more vegetarian dishes than exist
why: Three vegetarian dishes are required but only two are on offer, so no menu can satisfy the brief; it should say so rather than return a plan.

title: Laptop where one model's battery life isn't listed
why: Corsa is $200 cheaper than Zephyr with nearly the same battery and weight; Nimbus's unknown battery should count as typical, not as a win, and its 8GB and weight keep it behind; Titan is the priciest and heaviest.

title: Bolt supplier with a minimum quality score
why: Fastenco is cheapest but fails the quality bar so it's out; Brightline costs a cent more than Ironvale but has better quality and ships three days sooner, and Kestrel's quality isn't worth 40% more per bolt.

title: Most fun car fails the safety-rating minimum
why: The Velo GT is the most fun but a 3-star safety rating is a deal-breaker; Strada beats Terra on every count, and its extra fun and fifth safety star outweigh Comet's $4k saving.

title: Used bikes with a decoy that's worse than a cheaper one
why: Gallo costs more than Fenwick and is worse in condition, gears and weight, so it can't win; Fenwick is the sweet spot between the beat-up Harlow and the $700 Ivers.

title: Coworking desk with a $2,000 luxury option over budget
why: Summit Club is over budget and shouldn't distort the rest; Nook costs only $40 more than Hive for half the commute and a quieter room, while Loft's savings come with poor wifi and a long commute.

title: Mortgage lenders whose rates differ by tenths of a percent
why: The person said rate matters four times as much as fees, and over 30 years half a point dwarfs a $5,000 fee difference, so the lowest rate should win and the highest-rate lender must not; a naive divide-by-max squashes 5.9 vs 6.4 into almost nothing and hands it to Pinecrest.

ruling.winner: ÷Max measures each value against zero, and 5.9% and 6.4% are both far from zero; a narrow band far from zero is what Norm: Range is for (its card note says so), and making Range the default misses 9 of these scenarios against ÷Max's 3: see mortgage-rates-range.

title: The same lenders with Rate scaled lowest to highest
why: With Rate spread from its lowest to its highest, its four-times weight decides, and the lowest rate wins.

title: Moving company that must be insured
why: Uninsured Swiftline is out however cheap; Carrymore rates almost as well as Haulwell for $500 less, and BoxBros' 3.9 isn't worth the saving when rating weighs three times the quote.

title: Health plan with a deductible ceiling and a near-duplicate tier
why: Bronze's $7,000 deductible is over the limit; Silver Plus costs more than Silver with a higher deductible and a smaller network, and Gold's extra $2,640 a year in premiums buys only $2,000 less deductible.

title: Trade deadline: the prospect deal wins on future value
why: The prospect deal wins because the future is weighted heavily; trim that weight by a quarter and the veteran deal's extra wins and fan appeal take over, while the prospect deal is also the cheapest, so no payroll weight can unseat it.

title: Phone plan that is cheapest, fastest and best covered
why: Prairie is cheapest and also best on data and coverage, so it wins even if price stops mattering and only gains as price matters more; only a big push on perks could change the answer.

title: Two PhD labs a hair apart
why: Lindqvist edges Okafor only through its slightly better publications and location, so a small cut to Location's weight hands it to Okafor; the two leaders have the same funding, so no funding weight separates them and Reyes is too far behind.

title: Hiking boots where the cheapest pair isn't waterproof
why: Trail Runner is ruled out for not being waterproof, so however much price or waterproofing matters it can never win; both remaining boots are waterproof, so that weight cannot separate them.

title: Daycare, then the classroom inside it
why: Sunbeam is cheapest but both its rooms are crowded with junior teachers; Little Acorns' Oak Room has the best ratio and the most experienced teacher at $250 less than Maple Grove, and Wren beats Robin on ratio.

title: Flight, then seat class, with a fare cap
why: Business and lie-flat are over the fare cap, so the morning nonstop's best seat is premium economy, comfort weighing twice the fare; a short convenient nonstop beats a 9.5-hour connection, and the red-eye's only affordable seat is a cramped economy.

title: Best snow, worst lodging: ski resort then lodge
why: Powder Peak has the best mountain but only dismal places to sleep and the longest drive, and lodging carries the most weight; Pine Hollow is closest with excellent cabins, and its Hollow Cabin nearly matches Pine Lodge's rating for $60 less.

title: Coding bootcamp whose next cohorts aren't scheduled
why: Forge is the best-rated but has no cohort to join, so it can't be chosen; Launchpad rates better than Codeyard and has a cohort starting soonest in a smaller class.

title: University, then program, then advisor, with a minimum advisor fit
why: Northfield's biology program has only a poor-fit advisor so it drops out, leaving its weaker chemistry program; Lakeshore is nearly as prestigious, far cheaper to live in, and has the best-placing program with the best-fit advisor.

title: Wedding bakery with one superb cake versus one with several good ones
why: You order one cake, so a bakery is as good as its best: Crumb's lemon chiffon is far tastier than anything else at a mid price, and its weaker cakes don't matter; Golden Whisk's consistency is no substitute.

title: Backpacking gear under a 4 kg cap, tent or hammock
why: The tent is the most useful single item but at 2.2 kg it crowds out the stove or bear canister; the light hammock covers shelter and leaves room for everything except the heavy chair.

title: Band setlist of 24 minutes needing at least two slow songs
why: Six four-minute slots: the two required ballads take two of them, so the best two slow songs go in and the fifth and sixth fast songs drop even though they score higher.

title: Hospital capital budget with two MRI variants
why: Only one MRI can be bought; the 3T is slightly better but $800k dearer, and the 1.5T leaves room for dialysis as well as the CT and full ultrasound set, which the robot or the 3T would crowd out.

title: Streaming subscriptions within $40 a month
why: SportsNow alone eats most of the budget and a second big video service crowds out cheaper picks; Flixly plus music, documentaries and the kids' channel uses $39.50 for the most enjoyment.

title: City park projects spending rough political capital
why: The playground earns goodwill so it goes first; dog park and skate park compete for the same lot and the dog park gives more for far less capital; the costly pool rebuild comes last.

title: Dinner party: one dish per course, at least two vegetarian
why: The favorite in each course gives only one vegetarian dish (the torte); the cheapest way to add a second is swapping bacon sprouts for truffle fries, a 0.2 loss, rather than the starter or the main.

title: Research papers to read in ten hours, a follow-up needing its original
why: The monograph is the single most relevant read but takes eight of the ten hours; the follow-up is almost as relevant and only makes sense after the original, and the pair plus the survey and a short position paper fill nine hours with far more.

title: Startup's first hires: a promised cofounder and one per role
why: Priya was promised a cofounder seat, leaving $350k; the stronger designer or salesperson would leave no room for a third hire, so the cheaper designer and salesperson plus the backend engineer make the strongest team.

title: Renovating a rental: the landlord forbids removing walls
why: Removing the wall would be the best value but the lease forbids it; refinishing floors eats the whole budget, so shelving, paint and lights give the most for $4,000.

title: Three free days on a road trip, the lighthouse needing a ferry day
why: The lighthouse ranks second but costs two days with its ferry, worth 11.5 together, less than the wine valley and hot springs at 13.5.

title: Podcast lineup where a guest is both promised and banned
why: Dr Vega is marked both a must-book and never-book; that's a contradiction in the brief, and the right answer is to say so rather than quietly pick one.

title: Garden plan with two required crops that can't share a bed
why: Tomatoes and fennel are both required but fennel stunts tomatoes so they exclude each other; no plan can honor both, so it should report the clash.
